svg.text: 2+1 split, heal the partition, verify the Raft log catch-up

g.text: 3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, bind-mounted so data survives a restart.
SERVER_LIST = arcadedb-0:2434:2480,... quorum=majority (persistent: databases + replication bind-mounted)
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
Database and schema are written through the leader, which Raft carries to every follower.
CREATE VERTEX TYPE User, Photo - EDGE TYPE HasUploaded, FriendOf, Likes - UNIQUE_HASH / FULL_TEXT / GEOSPATIAL
The pre-partition state is asserted directly on every node.
A follower is isolated on purpose, so the majority keeps the leader it already has and no election is needed.
The majority keeps writing. The isolated node is not queried: its mapped port may be unreachable.
The isolated node is restarted so its gRPC channels are rebuilt instead of waiting out the backoff.
reconnectToNetwork(); stop(); start(); waitForContainerHealthy(90); new ServerWrapper(...)
There is no conflict resolution to do: the minority never accepted a write, so catching up is a pure replay.
until(restarted == majorityCount && leader == majorityCount && other == majorityCount) atMost 180s
Two siblings push the same shape further: three consecutive cycles, and a one-way isolation that resyncs.
multiplePartitionCycles() captures the stable count BEFORE each restart, to avoid reading during a re-election
